import pytest
from tornado.escape import recursive_unicode

def test_recursive_unicode_with_nested_structures():
    data = {
        b'key1': [b'val1', (b'val2', {'b'key3': b'val3'})],
        'key4': b'val4',
        5: b'val5',
    }
    result = recursive_unicode(data)
    assert isinstance(result, dict)
    assert result['key1'] == ['val1', ('val2', {'key3': 'val3'})]
    assert result['key4'] == 'val4'
    assert result[5] == 'val5'
    # Ensure original bytes are not present in the result
    assert all(not isinstance(k, bytes) for k in result.keys())
    assert all(not isinstance(v, bytes) for v in result.values())

def test_recursive_unicode_with_non_iterable_and_non_bytes():
    obj = 42
    result = recursive_unicode(obj)
    assert result is obj  # unchanged for non-iterable, non-bytes

    obj_str = "hello"
    result_str = recursive_unicode(obj_str)
    assert result_str is obj_str  # unchanged for string

def test_recursive_unicode_with_mixed_types_and_identity():
    data = [b'bytes', 123, {'nested': b'bytes2', 'list': [b'bytes3']}]
    result = recursive_unicode(data)
    assert isinstance(result, list)
    assert result[0] == 'bytes'
    assert result[1] == 123
    assert result[2]['nested'] == 'bytes2'
    assert result[2]['list'][0] == 'bytes3'
    # Ensure that non-bytes elements retain identity
    assert result[1] is 123
